system.summary: A homophonic one-word-per-group code, numbers 2-3839, shared with Van Dedem's 1789 French despatches; R1895 (1799) uses a different marked system.
system.sibling_key: none found; siblings R1947 and R2053 (1789) have French solutions in the same code
system.notes: Opening groups 2504 2604 2704 and frames 701 801 ... 301 401 501 601 look like nulls. The code does not sort alphabetically in any test.

prior_solution.where: R2120: the contemporary clear decipherment was filed as R2121. R2122 and R2131: none found.

conditions.human_role: The human supplied the target and the DECODE cookie.

solution.what: Fetched metadata and images for the 4 records and 10 sibling records named in the DECODE notes.
Sibling records R2121, R1947 and R2053 are marked decrypted; R2121 holds the same cipher pages as R2120 plus their full clear decipherment.
Searched DECODE key records; checked the undated Fagel key series R2842-R2852, which are large alphabetical Dutch codebooks and not this code.
Transcribed R2122 and R2131, and the R2121, R1947 and R2053 cipher pages and their solutions (two agents).
Found heavy homophony (de x36 in the clear text, no group used more than 11 times) and that only 52-58% of the target groups occur in any crib.
Tested an alphabetical code order against anchored words.
Hard-EM, then leave-one-out word aligners with restarts, over the cipher and decipherment pairs.
Treated the hundreds digit as a dummy (thousands digit + last two digits) and re-aligned.

Second pass (Feyseel Nur, PR #21): groups re-indexed as T*1000 + (H>=5)*500 + line*5 + (H mod 5); the crib values from R2121, R1947 and R2053 then follow alphabetical order within each 500-group block (Spearman 0.799 for five columns, against 0.351 numeric order and a permutation null p99.9 of 0.368; OpenAI Codex re-derivation in alpha/codex_review/).

R2122 and R2131 decoded with the 354-value table graded A/B/C plus alphabetical brackets for unknown groups (alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt): firm values on 123 of 301 non-null groups; the loan theme of R2122 agrees with R2121.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1895 (1799) is in a marked system of 2-3-digit groups with superscript marks, not the 1788-93 homophonic word code of R2120/R2122/R2131, so it is its own entry (dedem1799); the 1788-93 letters stay in dedem1788.

Catalogue audit: profile, page and README brought into line with the second pass (they still said 'not solved' and 'not alphabetical'); fraction of firm values measured from alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 130 tokens, 80 types, nl-modern order 4: reading -2.009 per letter; random keys -2.142 (z 2.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.651 (mean -1.684, z -10.0); annealer on the real text -1.702. Verdict: underdetermined.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked tx/ transcriptions (R2121 cipher = the two R2120 pages), the contemporary clear decipherment tx/R2121_clear.txt, and the graded partial decoding of R2122/R2131 in alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt; key = alpha/dedem_alpha_table.tsv.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt read group by group: R2122 (A+B 40%) and R2131 (16 of 46 firm) have holes in nearly every clause; only the clear passages read (docs/_check_reading.py: 4 of 113 sentences clean). Both relabelled decoded, not read. R2120 reads from its contemporary decipherment tx/R2121_clear.txt (continuous Dutch; reading_review A). Method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> read from existing decipherment (parts); fraction_read 0.41 -> 0.673 (R2120 groups of all three letters).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.009; polyphony 0.0; 178 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.702

outcome.method_basis: R2120 is read from its contemporary clear decipherment, filed as R2121 pp. 2-4; R2122 and R2131 decode only in part with the code layout recovered from the sibling decipherments (R2121, R1947, R2053), and do not build sentences.
outcome.notes: R2120 deciphered at the time (R2121). R2122 and R2131 decoded in part with the block-alphabetical table of the second pass (PR #21): 41% of groups have firm values. R1895 (1799) is a different system, split to dedem1799.

texts.label: R2120 (cipher pages re-photographed as R2121), Pera 22 Dec 1788
texts.summary: Van Dedem, Dutch ambassador at Constantinople, reports to Grand Pensionary Van de Spiegel the Porte's proposed loan of 7-8 million, secured on the revenues of Morea, Negropont, Salonica, Volos, Urfan, Cara Agatz, Damascus, Sorien and Rodosto and the tribute of Jenischeher, and suggests the Levant Directors or Hope & Co. take it up. The decryption is the contemporary clear decipherment filed as R2121.

reading_review.note: The contemporary clear decipherment (tx/R2121_clear.txt) reads as continuous Dutch: the Porte's proposed loan of 7-8 million and its securities. It is the decipherment of this cipher, not a separate clear letter, so R2120 reads from an existing decipherment; the low score is the word list's coverage of 18th-century Dutch spelling.

texts.label: R2122, "Duplicaat", Pera 15 Jan 1789
texts.summary: Two cipher blocks (258 groups) in a clear letter to Van de Spiegel, decoded in part with the block-alphabetical table of the second pass; the firm words (envoyé, Porta, negociatie, Republicq, Leening) are consistent with the loan theme of the R2121 crib. Values, not sense: the running reading is fragmentary.
texts.note: Graded decode (alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt): 40% of groups with a firm value, the rest alphabetical brackets or guesses, so nearly every clause has holes; only the clear passages of the letter read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R2131, Pera 9 Feb 1793
texts.summary: One cipher paragraph of 50 groups in a clear letter to Van de Spiegel, decoded in part (16 of 46 non-null groups firm); it names the Porte, an envoy, the war and the French, but the neutrality reading proposed in review is not established.
texts.note: 16 of 46 non-null groups firm; the neutrality reading is not established and no sentence can be built (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).
